Subject: Production latency spike + 5xx impacting checkout

Hi Redwood team,

We started seeing a spike in latency and an increase in 5xx errors on our checkout flows starting ~08:45 PDT. Error rate jumped from ~0.2% to 6.4% and p95 latency went from 320ms to >2.5s. This is directly impacting conversions.

We've pinned traces to a few requests and can share logs if helpful. Currently routing some traffic to a fallback region but that's causing geographic regressions. Can someone confirm receipt and give an ETA for mitigation? We need an update for our leadership ASAP.

Thanks,
Jordan

Subject: Re: Fwd: Production latency spike + 5xx impacting checkout

Hannah — initial technical findings and mitigations below.

Timeline summary (initial):
- 08:29 PDT: autoscaler change deployed to reduce cold-starts; new kernel selection algorithm enabled for LLM runtime 2.1.
- 08:41 PDT: small rollout of the kernel selector hit a subset of Dedicated nodes serving Acme.
- 08:46 PDT: KV prefix cache invalidation observed when model variant mapping updated; this caused higher per-request compute and longer KV cache warmups.
- 08:49 PDT: autoscaler incorrectly interpreted temporary latency as sustained load and spun up additional small instances, which amplified the cache warmup cost and produced backlog.

What we did (mitigation):
- Rolled back kernel selector change at 09:05 PDT for the affected pool.
- Manually warmed KV cache for the Acme model variants and pinned a small pool to keep cache primed.
- Adjusted autoscaler threshold to prevent reactionary scale-ups during short-lived spikes.

Current state (11:00 PDT): error rate down to ~0.6%, p95 latency ~450ms, throughput normalized. We are monitoring for 1–2h.

Attachments: timeline-metrics-20260514.csv (metrics export), log-snippet.txt (trace IDs), mitigation-notes.md

Next steps (post-incident):
- Full RCA write-up and draft customer-facing summary.
- Reliable rollback plan for kernel selector changes and a staged rollout with canary traffic split.
- Autoscaler tuning + circuit-breaker to avoid cascading scale events.

Dev
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@acme-corp.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme-corp.com>

Date: 2026-05-16 09:42 PDT
Subject: Draft RCA and apology — Acme incident May 14

Jordan / Priya —

First, I want to sincerely apologize for the disruption on May 14. We take these incidents very seriously. Below is a concise summary of our findings and immediate actions; Hannah will follow with the finalized RCA and tracked actions.

High-level cause:
- A recent runtime kernel-selection change combined with a KV cache invalidation path caused a transient but amplified load on the affected Dedicated pool. The autoscaler reacted to symptom (latency) rather than cause, triggering additional instances that prolonged cache warmup and increased 5xxs.

What we fixed immediately:
- Reverted the kernel-selector rollout for the Acme-serving pool.
- Performed targeted KV cache warming and pinned capacity to avoid cold-cache penalties while we assess safer rollout patterns.
- Implemented a temporary autoscaler bailout rule to avoid cascade scale-ups for short-lived spikes.

Planned corrective actions (summary):
1) Rollback-safe rollout process for kernel selector changes; implement canary percentage gating and automated rollback if key metrics degrade (owner: dev_patel, ETA: 2026-06-01).
2) Autoscaler circuit-breaker and hysteresis tuning to prevent scale amplification (owner: markus_klein/dev_patel, ETA: 2026-05-28).
3) Improve KV cache telemetry and add early-warning alerts for cache-miss storms (owner: marissa_cole, ETA: 2026-05-24).
4) Customer credit proposal (one week of reduced committed usage for Acme) and formal apology letter (owner: rachel_kim, ETA: 2026-05-18).

Next steps: Hannah will attach the complete RCA PDF and a JIRA board with tracked tasks. We propose a 30-minute postmortem call tomorrow 10:00 PDT to walk through and accept action items. Would that work for your team?

Regards,
Markus Klein
VP, Operations & Reliability
Redwood Inference

Jordan / Priya — thank you for your patience. Attached is the final RCA PDF with an event timeline, root cause analysis, and customer-facing summary. Key points below and concrete next steps we will track to closure.

Summary (short):
- Root cause: combination of a kernel-selection rollout that produced KV cache invalidation for some Dedicated nodes and an autoscaler configuration that amplified the transient load, causing elevated latencies and 5xxs.
- Impact: checkout latency p95 peaked >2.5s for ~22 minutes; error rate peaked at 6.4%; estimated lost conversions: internal estimate shared separately.
- Mitigation timeline: rollback + cache warm + autoscaler tweak reduced errors to ~0.6% within ~40 minutes.

Action items (owner, ETA, status):
- INF-4821: Implement canary gating + automated rollback for kernel-selector (owner: dev_patel, ETA: 2026-06-01, status: in progress).
- INF-4832: Autoscaler circuit-breaker + hysteresis tuning (owner: markus_klein/dev_patel, ETA: 2026-05-28, status: in progress).
- INF-4840: KV cache telemetry + early-warning alerts (owner: marissa_cole, ETA: 2026-05-24, status: todo).
- INF-4851: Customer remediation & credit proposal (owner: rachel_kim, ETA: 2026-05-18, status: pending review).

Tracking: we created a public-facing JIRA board for Acme tasks: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4821 (link above). I will post weekly status updates in this thread until all items are complete. Please let us know if you need any additional detail or a follow-up meeting.

Attachments: RCA-Redwood-Acme-20260516.pdf, timeline-metrics-20260514.csv

Apologies again — we appreciate Acme's partnership and will work to prevent recurrence.

Best,
